steps.prompt: Finish these: “My phone is ___ than my old one.” “This is the ___ day of the year.” What did you add to the describing word each time?
steps.placeholder: My phone is… This is the…

cards.title: Two things or more?
cards.body: A comparative compares two things: “Mia is taller than Leo.” A superlative picks the most of three or more: “Mia is the tallest in the class.” Comparatives often come with “than”; superlatives usually come with “the”.

cards.title: -er/-est or more/most?
cards.body: Short words (one syllable, and most two-syllable words ending in -y) add -er and -est: fast, faster, fastest; happy, happier, happiest. Longer words use more and most: careful, more careful, most careful. Use one way, never both: not “more taller” or “most biggest”.

cards.title: Spelling changes
cards.text:
big → bigger → biggest (one vowel + one consonant: double it)
nice → nicer → nicest (ends in e: just add -r/-st)
happy → happier → happiest (consonant + y: y becomes i)
cards.note: Read the word aloud with -er. If it sounds clumsy (beautifuller, excitinger), use more/most instead.

cards.title: Irregular comparisons
cards.text:
good → better → best
bad → worse → worst
far → farther → farthest
little → less → least
many/much → more → most
cards.note: These don’t follow the rules, so learn them by heart. “Gooder” and “baddest” are not words.

prompts: How do you decide between -er and more?
